5.title: Best Girl's Birthday
5.main_content:
It was Regan's birthday recently, so we went to go see The Mandalorian and Grogu with her mom. I haven't watched the TV series, so my expectations going into it was for more sequel-trilogy-area slop. I was pleasantly surprised, however, as this movie is divorced from the baggage of post-Disney corporate-extended-universe Star-Wars; not even one time did a character utter the words "Skywalker", "Palpatine" or even "light-saber".

Starting with the good, the use of puppetry for Grogu and some of the other smaller creatures was much more pleasing to watch compared to uncanny CGI ghouls of other recent Star-Wars media. The dynamic of Mando as the gruff mercenary, whose heart is melted by the purity of their chipper young companion of Grogu is a classic trope, but a well executed for this movie, as it creates compelling character motivations. The action sequences were well choreographed, making for an exciting watch, especially the big pit fight scene. Steve Blum made an unexpected, but very enjoyable appearance voicing a witty co-pilot for Mando, they have good chemistry and he's got a great voice for the role.

Next, the weird and the bad. First the weird: Jabba the Hut's son is voiced by a Seth Rogen Impersonator. I have no source to confirm this, but he sounds like 10% different than Seth Rogen, and has the same dude-bro cadence, its amazing he never did the laugh. As far as the bad, the pacing felt strange in the middle, as if the movie were two TV scripts stitched together with a 15 minute interlude. It could have been a bit smoother transitioning between the end of the first rescue mission and the start of the arc with the assassin. My biggest personal gripe was the scene where Mando's mask is removed, because in spite of Pedro Pascal's good looks, Mando is the kind of masked character who is extremely hot, but instantly loses all sex-appeal once they remove their mask/helmet (i.e., Master Chief, Zorro, any male Knight). Another issue me and Regan both had was with the IMAX theater, I don't know if I'm getting old, but it was far too loud at times, especially during the pre-movie ads (shocking). Also there were some scenes with extreme flashing lights which were a problem.

Overall it was a very enjoyable experience (especially since it was free), and a refreshing reminder that under the right circumstances, Star Wars can be good, actually. Happy Birthday Regan :3

7.title: The Amazing Digital Transgender Experience
7.main_content:
THE AMAZING DIGITAL CIRCUS FINALE SPOILER BELOW
=========================

I went to see The Amazing Digital Circus Finale in theaters last week and it absolutely blew me away. The story's commitment to telling a trans narrative is exactly what my soul needed in the terrifying climate of modern society for trans folk.

The theatrical showing includes both episodes 8 & 9 for a proper theatrical-length experience and it was well worth it. Getting to re-experience Caine's musical number on the big screen was a blast, especially with the high energy of the audience. You could tell everyone in the room really loved digital circus; there were even a few cosplayers which is always fun to see. The cliffhanger-ending of episode 8 leads very smoothly into episode 9, creating a very coherent experience. 

Episode 9 largely explores the idea of "what happens next?". The major threat of a wrathful Caine is gone, leaving the circus a corrupted mess in his wake, and Kinger confirms suspicions of the cast being digital copies of real people, meaning escape was never an option. With everyone at their lowest the gang splits up to attempt to cope with their new reality. This leads into a beautiful sequence of Kinger teaching Pomni how to conjure, as they slowly attempt to rebuild the cracks in the circus. Overtime, the rest of the members notice and join in, and for a moment, it feels like everything will okay; we can cope and we can rebuild. Then bang, another Jax blowup, not surprising given what we've seen in the last few episodes, so when he wanders off, I expected a follow-up scene with him breaking down, or one of the characters chasing after him. Instead, we get the gut-punch, near instant cut to abstracted Jax. No fanfare, no transformation sequence; we've already seen what it looks like so no time is wasted. He's there, and then he's gone. It feels so viscerally tragic, and really spoke to me as a trans women, because that is sadly how life is for many of us. One day you see her, and she's not doing well, and then the next time you hear about her she's dead.

This leads into the second act, Pomni's descent into abstracted-Jax. This sequence was an absolute blast, the dialogue was so funny and so perfectly on-point for deconstructing who Jax is. I can't stop saying "Real life is gay". I loved that piano-Jax was playing Daisy-Daisy, it feels trans-coded as fuck and is perhaps a nod at the fan interpretation of Jax's post-transition name being Daisy. The final sequence of acceptance brought me to tears. The use of Stevie Wonder's "Isn't She Lovely" was such a perfect way to convey the joy of trans acceptance, and has irreversibly, permanently changed my brain chemistry.

This sequence is then followed by Caine's return and transformation. I can't help but draw parallels between Jax's acceptance of transition and Caine's acceptance of his wrong doing and subsequent releasing of the blue-AI. I love how abstract and artsy the sequence is, it does such a wonderful job of showing Caine's journey without saying anything at all.

The finale was so perfectly bittersweet. Getting to see the real-life counterparts to the circus crew was extremely rewarding; the crowd popped off like crazy at this point. It provides a hopeful relief from the absolute tragedy of Jax. She was too late to accept herself in the circus, but the real her still has a chance, and seems to be making progress. I adore Jax's real-life counter part being played as a total boy-moding emo twink, and while I'm sure it will confuse many cisgender viewers, it felt very real to my lived experience as a trans women. Maybe IRL Jax isn't out publicly yet, but that's how it was for me at first, kept private, a secret for only me and a select few to know for my safety. More than anything its sweet to see her not just surviving but living and make genuine connections in contrast to her other self.

This finale and this series as a whole will always hold a special place in my heart, and while I'm sad to see it go, I'm incredibly happy with how it ended, and I wouldn't change anything about it. 10/10, Trans Women make the best art.

11.title: Stare too long into the abyss and it will stare right back
11.main_content:
Regan and I have been playing the Liminal Industries modpack for Minecraft 1.20 recently, and it's the most fun I've had with a mod pack.

The main Crux of the modpack is the application of the robust tech mod Create, in a world that generates the liminal hellscape of the backrooms. While these concepts may seem unrelated, the world effectively per-generates spaces which are perfect for setting up massive contraptions.

In addition to the unique gimmick, the design of the modpack is really effective. In spite of having 150+ mods, the modpack feels lightweight and does not struggle with performance, nor does it feel   bogged down by an over abundance of mods. Instead, progression is carefully gated to ensure players are forced to engage with and learn each different mod's systems slowly through natural progression. This leads to an experience more akin to skyblock where the limitations of available resources force player to become creative in acquiring new resources. For example, I've played many modpacks which included the Botania mod, but this is the first time I've ever taken the effort to learn how it works, as it opened up an avenues for getting  new resources.

The generation of backrooms terrain is also really impressive, leading to world's which inspires a nice mix of labyrinthine madness and bizarre, uncomfortable curiosity. This isn't for you. Etc., etc.

Overall great time, my only complaint is it's running our sleep schedules :p

13.title: A Tale of Two Revolutionary Girls
13.main_content:
Recently finished revolutionary girl Utena, both the series and the movie, and wow, what a ride.

Overall I really enjoyed both, but the movie really knocked it out of the park. It leans way harder into the surrealist feeling that the show carries itself with. I really love the disorienting way the backgrounds slide together, creating a labyrinthine appearance to the school. I was surprised at how much the movie deviated from the plot of the series, but it made for a much tighter narrative. It was also interesting seeing how more comedic elements of the series, namely Nanami and ChuChu were almost completely cut out (save for the bizarrely hilarious cow VHS scene). 

I was especially pleased to see how much darker the film was. The main series touches on elements of sexual abuse, sexual assault and suicide, while the film is not shy to dive head first into these topics which made a much stronger impact. The movie is also explicitly much gayer than the series which was a welcome surprise. Lesbians stay winning. 

The third act was a total jaw dropper. I did not expect the absolute insanity of the cars, but  it somehow works so well. The ending shot of Utena and Anthy riding away on the motorcycle is an incredible shot to end on and I love that even at the very end of the line, the show still leaves viewers guessing as to the true nature of reality.

Overall I'd rank the movie an easy 10/10, while I'd say the series gets a strong 8/10, with points removed mostly due to the show's pacing being a bit too slow in earlier episodes.

14.title: Akira in theatres... AND THE PROMS TOMORROW
14.main_content:
Saw Akira for the first time today. We wanted to see a movie, and it happened to be playing at the theatre which was great. Regan and I have both wanted to watch it for a while.

The animation was fantasitc (made even better by the theatrical viewing). I love how realistic the artstyle is, everyone looks like they could be an actual human being. The film has some pretty gorey moments too, which I wasn't expecting, but theyre bery well used to create shock. Tetsuo turning that guy to red mist was fucking crazy.

The film's writing was great too. I loved seeing all the anti-imperialist messaging. Kaneda makes for a great main character, he's cool and serious when the story calls for it, but also goofy enough to act as comic relief to all the crazy nuclear-bomb-child-torture stuff.

The ending was really cool too. I like that it builds from a typical action movie ending, into some real existential-body horror nightmare. The abstract visuals at the very end were a perfect conclusion. 

Really what can I say that hasn't already been said, its a classic for a reason, what a great movie.

15.title: A Wonderful Wedding
15.main_content:
The  wedding happened and it was wonderful. The actual service was perfectly short and sweet. The chapel was tiny, only enough for 6 pews. The windows were stained glass with lots of pretty imagery like a boat in the water and a progress flag in the shape of a heart. The main window depicted Elvis with some choice lyrics. 

The service only lasted about 30 minutes but it was beautiful. Made me a little jealous to be honest :3 No talk of God either thankfully. After the service we took photos before heading to the restaurant. It was pouring down rain so everyone had to rush from the chapel to a next door building for pictures. I've never seen so many umbrellas in Newfoundland.  Champagne was handed out during photos, but Regan drove so I drank both and got totally blitzed.

We went to a fancy seafood restaurant. It was named after a local hero, a captain who carried 20 people off of a sinking ship in the midst of a horrible storm. Apparently he was quite modest about it too. We sat with some friends of the groom, which was fun, they had a lot of funny stories to share. I got fried cod and mussel, which was tasty, but the mussel went cold too fast (not surprising for mussels though).
The next day was the reception. This is where the real fun begins. It started fairly traditional with everyone seated and the traditional familial dances. Then the fun started to ramp up when the dance floor opened. For the first time ever I felt like I got to properly enjoy dancing at a wedding (in no short thanks to copious amounts of booze). The spread of food was also amazing. Charcuterie of all kinds, fancy jams on crackers, Mini cheese cake with bake apple jam, lemon meringue pretzels, a candy bar and so much more I can't even remember. There was no formal catering; instead at 1130 the groom came around and to every table and handed out vouchers for a free poutine, followed by the Ziggy Peel Goods (a famous fries food truck) truck pulling up outside. It was perfect timing as everyone was already thoroughly drunk. Slowly we watched the dance floor die as people rolled out of the venue, and then back in with a big box of fries.

It was an absolute blast of a time, I've never had so much fun at a wedding.

16.title: After 20 years, Sonic and the Secret Rings is now playable
16.main_content:
Sonic project reignition is one of those rare fan projects which presents the opportunity to re-write history for a bad game. Similar to project 06, project reignition recreates the entirety of sonic and the secret rings from the ground up in Godot, allowing players to utilize a standard controller rather than Wii remote tilt controls. This change is more than enough to push the game from being a forgettable spin off of the 2000s to genuinely one of the best experiences I've had playing a 3D sonic game.

With proper controls, secret rings  boast fun level design, and an addictive feedback loop with its mission system. I initially expected the mission style gameplay to be grating, but most of the mission are well designed, and unlocking and customizing sonic skills proved to be especially exciting as a game mechanic. Speed brake and time break serve to spice up the gameplay compared to typical boost gameplay seen in contemporary titles like sonic unleashed. Being able to slow down without losing top speed with time break is an excellent way to add harder platforming without alienating new players, which speed break enables seasoned players to push their advantage in tougher missions. This combined with a huge selection of selectable skills (double jump, light speed dash, etc.) creates for a platform error with a surprising degree of expression of movement.

The game runs very well, and features very few bugs. I'm not sure if any up-scaling occurred in the process of making the game, but assets look great and come together to create very vibrant and exciting land shapes for Sonic to race through.

The story isn't groundbreaking by any means, but it works for what it is. Sonic is characterized as more arrogant in this game, something I feel the modern games could benefit from returning to. The dynamic between sonic and Shara is really fun too, I love their banter during levels. The bit with story characters being replaced by sonic characters is shallow but good for a few quick laughs. Erzaor Djinn doesn't leave a huge impact as a villain, but the final encounter with him makes up for it with spectacle.

On top of everything else, project reignition even features native mod support, meaning it's very easy to play as your favorite characters. I tried out a blaze mod which worked quite nicely. Project reignition is genuinely one of the most fun experiences I've had with a sonic game in recent memory, and given that it's a free project, everyone who likes sonic should give it a try.

17.title: TLDR: Game Fun Story Bad
17.main_content:
My GF and I finished our playthrough of Dying Light recently, including the DLC. What a truly incredible mixed bag of a game. As far as gameplay is concerned, it's an absolute blast. The combat and climbing mechanics have a nice degree of fluidity to them, and being able to employ them in an open world with friends makes for some really fun moments of you and your partner slaughtering massive hordes of zombies together. That said it does suffer from the junk of being a 360 game. Particularly, the parkour aspects can be occasionally unreliable (I.e., over shooting on a wall climb, falling to grab a ledge, grappling hook not grabbing) but when it works its a total blast. This is further elevated by the introduction of drivable cars in the DLC. The cars feel surprisingly deep, you can really feel the weight of the car being thrown around, and the damage system creates unique obstacles that must be accounted for, like driving on bald tires or a broken engine. Additionally the game boasts a day-night system with night time being extra dangerous as ultra tough zombies known as volatile swarm the streets, which can only really be defeated through the use of UV lights (or cheese strategies), which are limited in availability, creating for some tense encounters.

Unfortunately I do have some heavy criticism for the game as well. For starters, it suffers from the curse of the open world game. This is an issue with 90% of open world games, but it is worth noting; although the open world is fun to explore at first, it becomes a bit grating over time, especially when many of the games quests have you running the same few types of fetch quests over and over. Speaking of quests, this is another area where the game could stand to improve. Some of them are fun, in particular any that have you enter an enclosed space like a building or parking garage really spice up the pacing, however many of them consist of "travel to location x to talk to person y and receive item z" which gets old fast. These style of missions become grating very quickly and unfortunately make up a majority of the side quests in the game.

Easily the games biggest flaw is its writing. Not surprising for a 360 Era game I know. The premise of the game takes a political spin on a zombie outbreak in which Harran is turned into a quarantine zone, and you play as Kyle Crane, a US government operative sent in on a political mission. Your first mission involves burning a create of antidote to the zombie disease, which makes it seem like the game will deal with Kyle's morality vs. His duty to the government, but this plot point basically goes entirely unused. Rather than try and make a point about the nuanced nature of government and political evil, the game instead paints the government as cartoonishly evil villains and Kyle Crane as the ultimate savior of the people, which is just extremely boring.
In general the game struggles with maintaining a consisting tone for writing. Some missions feel like they're going for maximum melodrama ultra serious zombie media, while others feel like total clown shoes, and the worst part is the clown shoe writing is significantly better than the melodrama, in spite of the melodrama being the focus of the writing. This continues into the DLC, with the only really difference being the shift in setting from Urban Survival in the city to countryside survival with a mystery cult. The cult sucks by the way.

Both the main game and the DLC featured extremely underwhelming endings. For starters both endings force you into single player, which sucks when you spend the whole game in co-op, and the final sequence doesn't have any technical elements which would be difficult to implement in multi-player. The ending of the main game leans extremely heavily on QTEs which is abysmal dogshit, I was expecting a fun fight with the main villain, sort of shoot out or melee duel but actually you kind of just get nothing.
The DLC follows up on this by giving you a choice between two endings. Both of which are stupid. In one ending you end up in a stupid fist fight with the final boss, which is made especially annoying because the game really does not emphasize unarmed combat. The alternate ending sees Kyle teaming up with the final boss, and as a result just has no final boss fight. I'm not sure which is worse, but narratively speaking both endings are fucking stupid.

Overall Dying Light is a really fun game mechanically, and a blast to play with friends, just don't expect very much from the story, and you will have a good time.

20.title: CITY!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
20.main_content:
I've been watching through CITY and what a genuinely delightful anime. I read a little bit of the manga years ago, but just like with Nichijou, the adaption seriously elevates the experiences.

For starters I am absolutely in love with the visual style. Whereas Nichijou pushes for a more pastel color palette, CITY leans into an extremely colorful artstyle with all colors fully-saturated. 

I'm very impressed with Arawi's ability to write such a huge ensemble cast. Nichijou uses a wide swath of characters, but many of them feel more one note (which works for Nichijou). Instead, CITY puts just enough focus on all the citizens to really succeed in feeling like the show is about all of the residents of CITY.

I haven't finished it yet, but in particular I wanted to highlight the friendship between Makabe and Amakazari. They have such explosive chemistry together, making for gut bustingly hilarious moments and bits that are almost difficult to keep up with. This is then further Augmented by the conflict of Amakazari moving away. The scene where she keeps trying to tell Makabe, and you can tell Makabe already knows but is in denial and so she clings desperately go their bits, hoping that they keep things as they are, tearfully pushing through gag after gag trying to stop her best friend from saying the words she never wanted to hear. I was in tears. Regan didn't really get it, which is fair given the actual contents of the scene 🎃.

Once again Keiichi Arawi delivers on an absolute master piece with a master class adaptation by the legendary KyoAni.
